articles.title: The Discovery of Comet Machholz (Comet 2004 Q2)
articles.summary: Don Machholz recounts his discovery of Comet C/2004 Q2 (Machholz) on August 27, 2004, detailing his methodical visual comet hunting approach using a 6-inch reflector and various verification methods. The narrative highlights the persistence of amateur astronomers in an era of automated sky surveys and the process of official comet confirmation. The article also provides a calendar of events for the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: James Lick
articles.summary: James Lick, born in 1796, led an unusual life, starting as a carpenter and piano maker before building a fortune through successful businesses in South America and subsequent land ownership in California during the Gold Rush. At 77, advised by astronomer George Davidson, Lick decided to dedicate his wealth to funding a great astronomical observatory. This resulted in the famed Lick Observatory on Mt. Hamilton, where he is interred beneath the pier of its 36-inch refractor telescope.

articles.title: Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series
articles.summary: Apollo 9 astronaut Russell Schweickart is scheduled to deliver a non-technical, illustrated lecture titled "Asteroid Deflection: Hopes and Fears" on October 6, 2004, at Foothill College in Los Altos Hills, California. The free public event, part of the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series, will cover the threat of cosmic rocks and methods for protecting Earth from asteroid impacts. Schweickart, also chairman of the B612 Foundation, will discuss both nuclear and non-nuclear deflection alternatives.

articles.title: Solar System Stats for October 2004
articles.summary: This document provides an astronomical ephemeris for October 2004, detailing key statistics for planets in our solar system (Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) and the Sun. For specific dates within the month (1st, 11th, 21st), it lists their Right Ascension, Declination, distance from Earth in Astronomical Units, apparent magnitude, and apparent angular size. The data is adapted from the Observer's Handbook published by The Royal Astronomical Society of Canada.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: This document outlines the status of the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) loaner telescope program for its members. It provides contact information for borrowing scopes and lists various telescopes currently available, those out on loan with due dates, and scopes with extended loan periods. A waiting list for popular items is also included, detailing different types of telescopes such as Dobsonians, Newtonians, and Schmidt-Cassegrains.
